clue.text: Clear account and retire

parts.note: to retire from a job is to quit it

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper settles the books and steps down from the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone of a charge is to find them not guilty, a verdict-giving synonym.

clue.text: Info often enclosed, giving indemnity to landlords?

definitions.meaning: the explanatory notes slipped into an envelope with a CV or application
read whimsically: insuring, or providing cover for, people who let out property

explanation.surface: An insurance mailing sent to landlords comes with the usual explanatory paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: COVERING (insuring) the LETTERS, people who let rooms or houses; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Job applications and documents are usually sent with a short explanatory note on top, so these are info that is often enclosed.

clue.text: Anonymous nude man sculpted

indicators.note: something sculpted is shaped into a new form, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A statue of a naked man has no name attached to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something anonymous has no name given, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Club's empty restaurant served up meal without starter

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means written bottom to top, so read backwards
an empty word has had its inside removed, leaving only its outer letters
without its starter means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a luncheon is a formal midday meal

explanation.surface: A club's restaurant stands empty, and the meal it serves lacks a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves RT from restaurant, and 'served up' turns that to TR; 'without starter' drops the L from LUNCHEON, leaving UNCHEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer's short heavy stick is a type of club or cudgel.

clue.text: Dashed after Euro-politician's returned for part of Wales

indicators.note: after places the word for dashed behind the politician
returned means sent back, so the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: an MEP is a Member of the European Parliament
dashed hopes are broken ones; broke is the past form

explanation.surface: A Euro MP comes back from Brussels, crestfallen, to a Welsh constituency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashed' looks like an adjective about mood, but supplies BROKE, as in dashed or broken plans; the clue's 's is a link meaning 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pembroke is a town in south-west Wales, giving its name to Pembrokeshire, so a part of the country.

clue.text: Controversial European music putting US off

parts.note: a Pole is a European, someone from Poland

indicators.note: putting, together with off, means setting aside, so the named letters are removed
off completes 'putting off', telling us to remove letters from the word for music

parts.note: US is taken as written, the two letters to drop

explanation.surface: Some divisive Continental music fails to land with American listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European' is a person here, not an adjective qualifying music.
explanation.definitionFit: A polemic is a fierce argumentative attack, and as an adjective means contentious or disputatious.

clue.text: Nutmeg's run into by learner — called AA initially

indicators.note: run into by means the second item is put inside the first

parts.note: Nutmeg is the setter, so what belongs to Nutmeg is mine
L is the learner sign on a British L-plate

explanation.surface: The setter's work gets an unwelcome visitor from a novice driver.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a person whose initials were A.A.: the author of Winnie-the-Pooh, Alan Alexander Milne.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winnie-the-Pooh author signed himself with the initials A.A., so he was called AA initially.

clue.text: Refuse two bachelors, one in haste

indicators.note: in places the bachelors and one inside the word for haste

parts.note: haste is a rush
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA, so two give BB
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Two single men turn down an offer, one of them in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse, said REF-use, is waste matter or garbage, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Sign by restricted area, advice to those in rehab?

definitions.meaning: the notice on a lawn in a park that walkers must not cross
grass is slang for cannabis, so recovering users are told to stay away from it

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes grass as slang for cannabis, the drug people in rehab are steering clear of.
explanation.definitionFit: Park lawns carry this notice to stop walkers trampling them, and the words also urge drug users to abstain.

clue.text: Final episode unable to be shown regularly

parts.note: an episode is an incident or event

indicators.note: shown regularly means only every other letter appears, starting from the first

explanation.surface: The last episode of a TV series cannot go on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown regularly' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of 'unable', giving UAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventual means coming at the end of a process, ultimate or final.

clue.text: Editor behind contracted group pressuring cast

indicators.note: behind places the editor after the other piece
contracted means shortened, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a lobby is a group pressuring politicians

explanation.surface: An editor follows a shrunken pressure group as it campaigns over the casting of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To lob is to throw or toss, so lobbed is a past-tense synonym for cast as in thrown.

clue.text: Lip, bloody lip!

parts.note: B is the printed euphemism for bloody, as in 'b-- awful'
the lip of a cup or bowl is its rim

explanation.surface: An exasperated parent snaps at a child's cheek: 'Lip, bloody lip!'
explanation.walkthrough: The repeat makes the clue look like an exclamation about cheek; the first lip is the definition and the second gives RIM.
explanation.definitionFit: The lip of a glass or a hat is its upper edge, a synonym for the projecting rim.

clue.text: Player with little French put into cold changing room

indicators.note: put into places the French word inside the other letters

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: changing means being altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: petit is French for little

explanation.surface: A sportsman with a smattering of French is put in the chilly changing room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing room' looks like a single place, but 'changing' is an anagram signal working on the word after it, and 'put into' splits the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor takes part in a contest or game, so is a player.

clue.text: Tense concerning 11

parts.note: on means about or concerning, as in a book on birds
the cross-reference points to the clue at 11 across, whose answer means a lip, i.e. an edge

explanation.surface: A grammar question about the tense used in another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like grammar, but it is the adjective meaning nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on edge is nervous and keyed up, an idiom for anxious.

clue.text: Male introduced to change rear part of motor

indicators.note: introduced to means placed into the next word

parts.note: change is coins, cash
aft means at the back or rear of a ship

explanation.surface: A man is brought in to alter the back end of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' and 'rear' look like verbs about a car, but give CASH and AFT.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating shaft carrying the cams that open an engine's valves is a component of a motor.

clue.text: Gathering has to take only its fourth call

parts.note: must means has to

indicators.note: only its fourth means just the fourth letter of the preceding word is used

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: A gathering is told to accept only its fourth phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustering means assembling troops or people, so it is a gathering together.

clue.text: Female leading feeble corporal, perhaps, in dance

indicators.note: leading places the female in front

parts.note: a lame excuse is a feeble one
a corporal is one example of an NCO, a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A woman takes the lead in a dance with a weak soldier as partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is the passionate Spanish dance of Andalusian gypsy origin.

clue.text: Mum putting a bloke in the shade

indicators.note: putting means placing, here describing the insertion
in places the bloke inside the word for mum

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum
a gent is a man or bloke

explanation.surface: A mother leaves a man in the shade, outshining him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the shade' suggests eclipse, but 'shade' alone is the definition, a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a purplish-red colour, and a shade is a particular hue.

clue.text: Our best buckles not so smart

indicators.note: something that buckles bends out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Our best effort gives way, showing we were not so bright after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means dull-witted, so the comparative form means less clever.

clue.text: Quiet woman, at heart excessively contrary

indicators.note: at heart means placed in the middle of the word for woman

parts.note: she refers to a woman

indicators.note: contrary means turned the opposite way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: too means excessively, as in too much

explanation.surface: A calm woman who is, deep down, terribly perverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quiet' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb, to calm; 'contrary' turns OOT around, and 'at heart' places it in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To quiet a crying baby is to calm it, a verb synonym for soothe.

clue.text: Front of brochure primarily poet's work

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so the first letters of the words are used

parts.note: a poet writes verse

explanation.surface: The front of a brochure mainly carries a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' reads as a link, but its first letter is needed with that of 'brochure'.
explanation.definitionFit: The obverse of a coin or medal is its front face, the side bearing the head.

clue.text: Eg, seat belt adjusted for six-footer

indicators.note: adjusted means altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seat belt is adjusted for a very tall passenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person, but means an insect with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects have six legs, so this large horned beetle is a six-footer.

clue.text: Relaxed dressmaker turning up in odd places

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading from the bottom, backwards
the odd places are the 1st, 3rd, 5th letters and so on of the word

explanation.surface: A dressmaker, calmer now, shows up in strange spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in odd places' takes DESAE from dressmaker; 'turning up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means loosened or made less tense, a synonym for relaxed.

clue.text: Star having first of her five a day?

parts.note: the five-a-day health rule asks for five portions of fruit and veg, so the first can be a veg

explanation.surface: A celebrity eats the first of her recommended daily portions of fruit and vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: Five a day is the health advice to eat five portions of fruit and vegetables daily; one such portion, a VEG, then A, with 'day' completing the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra, one of the brightest in the night sky.

clue.text: Game, part of it inspiring local backs

indicators.note: backs means goes backwards, so the whole is reversed
inspiring means breathing in, so one word takes the other inside

parts.note: 'it' is the game, and a set is a part of a match
a local is a pub, an inn

explanation.surface: A game in which a pub team's defenders are motivated.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion gives SINNET, which 'backs' turns round; 'it' points back to the game being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, an example of a game.

clue.text: Cock-up — general initially missing part of motorway complex

parts.note: a slip is a blunder or cock-up

indicators.note: initially missing means its first letter is dropped

parts.note: broad means general, as in broad terms

explanation.surface: A blunder leaves a general without directions at a motorway junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' looks like an army officer, but is the adjective meaning broad.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip road is the short link road leading on to or off a motorway at a junction.

clue.text: Man's man possibly wiser to go without wife across country

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so the shortened word surrounds the other
to go without means to lose, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a country is a land

explanation.surface: A man who has lost his wife may be wiser travelling the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man, so a Man's man is a Manx resident; 'possibly' because other islanders count too.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from the Isle of Man is one example of someone living on an island.

clue.text: Unctuous Farmer George given a piece of cake

parts.note: Farmer George was the nickname of King George III, and GR stands for Georgius Rex
a piece of cake is something easy

explanation.surface: An oily farmer called George is handed a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: Farmer George was the nickname of George III, who took a keen interest in agriculture; his royal cipher is GR.
explanation.definitionFit: Unctuous literally means oily, so greasy is a synonym in its physical sense.
